lines: Trigger generator whose pulses arrive at random intervals, drawn from the exponential distribution that describes radioactive decay, at an average rate you set
Sets the average number of triggers per second, from 0.0001 to 100, marked in becquerels
At 0% the interval to the next trigger is drawn fresh each time and varies widely; at 100% every interval is the same length, which turns the output into an even clock at the rate set by RATE
Scales the rate set by the RATE knob, and reads 10V when nothing is patched: 5V halves the rate, and 0V or any negative voltage stops the triggers altogether
Nothing in the module reads this jack; the spacing of the triggers comes from the STABILITY knob alone, despite the maker's tooltip calling it Stability CV
A 1ms pulse at 10V, one for each trigger
Note — the module runs from its own timing, so it produces triggers with nothing patched into it.
Note — the green lamp flashes on each trigger, and holds at half brightness whenever the rate has fallen to zero and no triggers are being produced.

src/Tritium.cpp:62 and 64 call setVoltage(10) and setVoltage(0) on channel 0 only, gated by a dsp::PulseGenerator whose default duration is 1e-3 seconds (Rack-SDK include/dsp/digital.hpp:189)

Tritium.notes:
The Stability CV input is declared, given a panel jack and named by the maker, but is read nowhere in process(): getStability() at src/Tritium.cpp:38 returns the parameter alone. It is therefore given a line saying so and no family, since a colour would say something can be patched there.

The rate is a product, not a sum: rate = 10^knob * volts/10, so the jack scales the knob rather than adding to it, and the knob alone is what is heard when the jack is unpatched (the normal is 10V, which makes the multiplier 1).

The interval between triggers is stability-weighted: (1-s)*period + s, where period is a fresh -log(uniform) draw, so stability blends the exponential draw toward a fixed interval of one over the rate.

lines: Two knobs, each holding a steady voltage at its own jack, for offsets and for setting another module's CV input by hand
Sets the voltage carried by OUT 1, -10V to +10V
Carries the voltage set by the CONST 1 knob, -10V to +10V, with no smoothing or slew
Sets the voltage carried by OUT 2, -10V to +10V
Carries the voltage set by the CONST 2 knob, -10V to +10V, with no smoothing or slew
Note — the two halves are wholly separate: neither knob or jack has any effect on the other.

Lead.notes:
Read from the repository at commit 414e488, the tip of the default branch; every commit in the repository carries version 2.0.0 in plugin.json, so the installed build cannot be narrowed further than that.

The repository holds a Carbon.svg panel in res/ and assets/, but no Carbon source file and no Carbon model in plugin.json, so there is no third module.
